title: Basic English — Course 1, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 10

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Where will the group meet?
tasks.audioText: Our English group is organising a visit to the airport training centre next month. We are going to meet at the college entrance at half past eight. The bus will leave at nine sharp. Please bring your student card and wear comfortable shoes. The centre has asked us to send the final list of visitors by Friday, so tell me today if you want to join.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. When must students say if they want to join?

tasks.prompt: Reading 1. Read the text. Aisha invites her classmates to a study session before the English test. She suggests meeting in the library on Tuesday at three. Two students cannot attend at that time, so the group checks everyone's timetable and agrees to meet on Wednesday instead. Aisha sends a message with the new time and asks everyone to bring their notes. Why does the group change the meeting day?
options: Two students cannot attend on Tuesday

tasks.prompt: Reading 2. What does Aisha ask everyone to bring?
Choose the correct future form: 'We ___ the airport training centre next month.'
Choose TWO useful details to include in an invitation.
Complete: 'A message asking someone to come to an event is an ___.'
You cannot attend an invitation. What is a polite reply?
options: Thank you for inviting me, but I can't come on that day.

tasks.prompt: Put the following steps for arranging a group meeting in a logical order.
Write 60–80 words inviting a classmate to a study session or college event. Include the date, time, place, purpose and a polite way to ask for a reply.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the invitation includes date, time, place and purpose (0–2); it contains a polite request for a reply and makes the next step clear (0–2); future arrangements and basic grammar are understandable (0–2); invitation/event vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
